verdict.rationale: Render documents itself as a managed cloud application platform. It offers git-push deploys, Blueprint YAML for full multi-service architectures, managed databases and load-based autoscaling, which covers the 'full-stack apps with no servers to manage' half of the story. The evidence never describes serverless functions as such; the closest item is Workflows SDK task definitions, which are not shown to be function-as-a-service deployment. Missing for 10: explicit serverless function deployment, documentation that the platform is serverless or has no infrastructure to manage, independent hands-on corroboration of zero-ops full-stack deploys.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy serverless functions and full-stack apps with no servers to manage

citations.quote: Render (https://render.com) is a cloud application platform for deploying, securing, and scaling applications
Connect your repo and ship with every push.
Define, deploy, and version your entire architecture with a single YAML file.
Load-based autoscaling that handles 100x traffic bursts and beyond
Deploy fully-managed databases with point-in-time recovery, read replicas, and high availability.
